narrative.overview:
Baalam-Nah is documented like a field record that happens to be alive: monumental names, precise coordinates, folio indexes, route traces, and practical entries sit directly against documentary photographs of the lagoon and property. The system is confident and place-specific rather than resort-polished. Water is both the subject and the organizing device.

Its visual rhythm moves between immersive photographic fields and emphatic blocks of cyan, yellow, paper, and deep blue. Editorial asymmetry, oversized type, square-edged panels, and sparse map notation keep the experience grounded in evidence while giving it a recognizable authored voice.
keyCharacteristics: Monumental condensed display type paired with plainspoken body copy and monospaced field labels.
Documentary photography used at architectural scale, never as incidental decoration.
Route lines, coordinates, folio indexes, captions, and ledger rows as recurring information devices.
Hard-edged color fields and offset structural shadows rather than soft lifestyle styling.
Responsive compositions that preserve hierarchy while changing from grids to stacked or horizontal-snap sequences.

rules.name: The Field Mark Rule
rules.body: Cyan and yellow behave as map annotations and signals; use them decisively, not as ambient decorative gradients.

rules.name: The Water Leads Rule
rules.body: Deep blue establishes the world, but real lagoon photography is the strongest color field whenever credible imagery is available.

rules.name: The Three Registers Rule
rules.body: Archivo Black names the place, Manrope explains it, and Recursive records it. Do not exchange their jobs.

rules.name: The Monument and Note Rule
rules.body: Large headings should feel nearly architectural; supporting labels should remain compact enough to read as notation.

rules.name: The Placed Paper Rule
rules.body: Offset shadows belong to ledger-like objects and tactile actions, never to every content surface.

dos: Do let original photography occupy full sections or substantial grid areas.
Do pair each expressive composition with practical information, labels, or a clear action.
Do use route traces, rules, captions, and coordinates when they organize genuine place-based information.
Do maintain full Spanish and English behavior without shrinking the intended hierarchy.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: Don't round panels, actions, labels, or image frames into generic hospitality components.
Don't substitute stock eco-resort imagery or decorative tropical motifs for documentary evidence.
Don't use yellow or cyan as unstructured decoration; each bright mark should signal, locate, or separate.
Don't flatten repeated photographs into equal cards when an uneven editorial sequence can tell the story.
Don't style X-Hazil Sur or Maya community context as exotic texture; keep historical notes sourced, restrained, and legible.
